historical_timeline.summary: Published On Coca after experimenting with cocaine himself.
Irregular heartbeat attributed to smoking by his physician friend; failed attempts to stop smoking.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the palate: excision in April and radiation, then a radical operation by Hans Pichler with an obturator; kept smoking.

claims.statement: In 1894, at 38, his friend the physician Wilhelm Fliess attributed his irregular heartbeat to smoking and told him to stop. He tried repeatedly and failed: one attempt ended within seven weeks, and a later one lasted fourteen months before he started again, describing the abstinence as torture.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Treating tobacco dependence in a man who has already had a smoking-related cancer, without judgment: primary care for a 74-year-old physician and writer, seven years after a partial maxillectomy for squamous cell carcinoma of the palate, who still smokes about twenty cigars a day after many failed attempts to stop. The episode covers an assessment of readiness that does not blame him; starting varenicline before he is ready to set a quit date and adding combination nicotine replacement (ATS 2020, USPSTF 2021), with the point that cigars count; behavioral support; the risk of second primary cancers; head and neck cancer survivorship (NCCN, ACS 2016): yearly examination after five years, imaging only for symptoms or as screening supports, and lung cancer screening eligibility when the history is of cigars rather than cigarettes; maxillofacial prosthodontic care of the obturator, with speech, swallowing and dental care; nutrition and weight; and chronic pain managed without long-term opioids (CDC 2022). There is no radiation in the synthetic history, so there is no osteoradionecrosis risk.

visit_schedule.purpose: Establishing primary care seven years after maxillectomy for palatal cancer: about twenty cigars a day, a worn obturator, pain and weight loss
Two-week review with the maxillofacial prosthodontics consultation: obturator reline, speech, swallowing and dental care; varenicline at full dose
Six-week review: smoking down by two thirds, setting a quit date, pain and weight
Twelve-week review: five weeks without smoking, the new obturator and survivorship surveillance
Same-day sick visit for Candida stomatitis under the obturator
Five-month review: abstinence, lung and aortic screening results, pain, weight and the survivorship plan

hpi.narrative: Mr. Freud returns two weeks after intake and is seen by Dr. Vasquez-Lindqvist of maxillofacial prosthodontics on the same day. He finished the varenicline starter week and has taken 1 mg twice daily for a week. He has mild nausea when he takes it before breakfast and vivid dreams, and no change in mood. He now smokes about fourteen cigars a day, from twenty, and says the cigars are less satisfying. He is not yet ready to name a quit date but thinks it may be possible within a month. He has not called the quitline. His pain is unchanged at 6 of 10 on acetaminophen 1,000 mg three times daily. Liquids still leak into his nose at times.

referral.question: Worn obturator seven years after a right partial maxillectomy for palatal squamous cell carcinoma, with pain where it rubs, hypernasal speech, nasal leakage of liquids and weight loss, in a 74-year-old man who smokes about twenty cigars a day. Please assess and treat the prosthesis and advise on speech, swallowing and dental care
referral.urgency: Within two weeks, on the same day as his two-week primary care visit
referral.pertinent_history: Squamous cell carcinoma of the right hard and soft palate seven years ago, treated by right partial maxillectomy with clear margins (pT2 N0) and no radiation; definitive obturator made at the time and never replaced; yearly surveillance by his head and neck surgeon with no recurrence, last examination ten months ago. About twenty cigars a day for about fifty years. Pain 6 of 10 at the defect margin and right cheek; liquids leak into his nose; speech hypernasal; weight down 4 kg in six months to 58.4 kg, albumin 3.4 g/dL, hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL. No allergies. Started today: varenicline (before a quit date), scheduled acetaminophen 1,000 mg three times daily, a soft high-protein diet with supplements
questions: Can the obturator be relined or adjusted now, and does he need a new one?
Is the sore area at the defect margin caused by the prosthesis, or does anything need a biopsy or his surgeon's review?
What can be done for his speech and the nasal leakage of liquids?
What dental and prosthesis care do you advise for his remaining teeth and the defect?
Which form of nicotine replacement works best with an obturator, and how does smoking affect the prosthesis and the tissues?

consultant_note.history: Mr. Freud, a 74-year-old physician and writer, is seen at the request of Dr. Reinholt. Seven years ago he had a right partial maxillectomy for palatal cancer, without radiation, and has worn the same obturator since. Over the past year it has loosened; liquids leak into his nose when he drinks, his speech becomes nasal as the day goes on, and a sore spot at the front of the defect hurts when he chews. He cleans the obturator by rinsing it and wears it day and night. He has smoked about fourteen cigars a day this week, down from twenty, on varenicline. He has not noticed any lump or bleeding
consultant_note.data_reviewed: Dr. Reinholt's intake note and today's two-week note. Weight 58.2 kg today, from 58.4 kg; albumin 3.4 g/dL and hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL at intake. Surveillance letter from his head and neck surgeon ten months ago: no recurrence

exam.finding: Right partial maxillectomy defect with a healthy lining; 4 mm shallow ulcer with a clean base at the anterior margin where the flange presses; no induration, mass, or white or red patch; remaining upper and lower teeth with tobacco staining and two areas of root caries
Acrylic obturator worn, porous and stained, with a gap at the posterior lateral seal and an overextended anterior flange
Hypernasal resonance and audible nasal emission with the obturator in; better after the reline
No lymph nodes felt

assessment.display: Worn obturator with a poor seal
assessment.assessment: After seven years the acrylic is worn and porous and the tissues have changed, so the bulb no longer seals at the back. A chairside reline with a soft tissue conditioner restores the seal for now, but a new definitive obturator is needed

assessment.display: Pressure ulcer at the defect margin
assessment.assessment: A shallow ulcer under an overextended flange, with no induration or mass, is a pressure ulcer. The flange was relieved today. It should heal within two weeks; if it does not, his head and neck surgeon should see it and take a biopsy, because new or persistent lesions in a smoker with a past oral cancer may be a recurrence or a second primary

Both come from the poor seal and improved at once with the reline. A short course of speech-language therapy, starting now with the relined obturator and continuing after the new one is fitted, will help him use it well

assessment.display: Dental care, nicotine replacement and smoking
assessment.assessment: He has two areas of root caries and a high caries risk. Smoking stains and roughens the acrylic, encourages Candida, slows healing and raises the risk of a second cancer in the mouth. Nicotine gum sticks to acrylic, so a lozenge, dissolved on the side away from the defect, is better; the patch has no effect on the prosthesis. No radiation was given, so there is no risk of osteoradionecrosis and extractions can be done in the usual way if needed

recommendations: Chairside reline with a soft tissue conditioner and relief of the anterior flange done today
New definitive obturator: impressions in about four weeks and fitting about six weeks later
Recheck the ulcer in two weeks; his head and neck surgeon and a biopsy if it has not healed
Speech-language therapy sessions to improve resonance and swallowing with the relined and then the new obturator
Brush the obturator twice daily, soak it overnight in a denture cleanser, and leave it out for at least six hours each night once the new one fits well
High-fluoride toothpaste at night, treatment of the two root caries, and dental cleaning every three months
Nicotine lozenge rather than gum, and the patch, are both suitable with the obturator; stopping smoking will protect the tissues and the prosthesis
consultant_note.communication: Discussed with Dr. Reinholt, who sees him the same day. The plan was explained to Mr. Freud, who agreed and chose to have the impressions taken before his summer schedule
consultant_note.follow_up: Prosthodontics clinic for impressions in about four weeks and fitting of the new obturator about six weeks later, then a check one month after fitting and yearly; Dr. Reinholt continues tobacco treatment, pain care and survivorship care
